propositions: Concurrent reducer cache writers use a fixed `.cache.json.tmp` temp file, allowing one writer to rename it into place while another continues mutating the now-visible final file.
A cache hit can return a current-hash envelope with stale state fields spliced from a different event generation when concurrent writers observe different generations.
The `write_cache` function and corrupt-CREATE handling in `process_create` both publish cache independently, violating atomic publication and deterministic replay invariants.
Cache invalidation tests fail because concurrent reductions of different event generations can publish coherent hashes with incoherent state without cache bypass.
Serialized (non-concurrent) cache writes produce no false hits, confirming the defect is strictly concurrency-driven.
